answer: Burst test: at a random second set by a public beacon, every ID gets the same ~2k-token inference job, due in 90 s (proposed). One agent on its own hardware finishes in ~20 s (est.). A farmer running 300 IDs on one GPU must queue them, so replies land in a staircase of evenly spaced finish times; IDs on one staircase share one payout. Like a lantern swung in a dark yard, the burst shows shared shadows. It rests on basalt-hard physics: hardware can't fake parallelism it doesn't own. Measured: nothing yet; tune by false-link rate.
